## Meaning of support

Allowed means an intended review candidate in `ecosystems.json`, not verified compatibility with every host/model. Skipped means no approved candidate placement. Shipped platform sources remain independently maintained. File existence and deterministic generation verify repository structure only, not installation or native behavior.

Declarations: [`master-skills/travel-itinerary/ecosystems.json`](https://github.com/mickpletcher/AI-Skills/blob/main/master-skills/travel-itinerary/ecosystems.json); capabilities: [`master-skills/travel-itinerary/capabilities.json`](https://github.com/mickpletcher/AI-Skills/blob/main/master-skills/travel-itinerary/capabilities.json).

### Scope of Yes ratings

- **OpenAI ChatGPT:** Yes for the recorded passing bounded ChatGPT instruction-packet cases only, with explicit native-host metadata. Current instruction bytes match a recorded passing case for this skill; installed routing, full workflow coverage, all resources and broader models remain unverified. See per-skill evidence below.

**Compatibility:** Yes requires actual evidence for an explicitly defined support scope; No requires a demonstrated incompatibility and a documented blocker. Unknown means affirmative scoped compatibility has not been established. A Yes applies only to its scope immediately above, never whole-skill or ecosystem-wide certification. Unknown also covers evidence needing additional host/case tracing; historical results remain below. Unknown does not mean incompatible, and skipped placement is not a technical blocker. No demonstrated host incompatibility is established here, so no No rating is assigned.

**Implementation status:** Implemented means an existing same-name repository variant (candidate, shipped source or scaffold), not installed, activated or natively verified. The detailed paths below identify which kind. Planned means explicit intent for this master but no variant yet. Not targeted means no existing variant or per-master target intent. Reserved product folders alone do not make every skill Planned.

The first seven rows are the existing repository target IDs. The additional five rows cover explicitly distinguished Microsoft products and reserved product guides, not new target approval or every AI product in existence. Amazon Q Developer is not Amazon Bedrock Agents; Grok consumer and Grok Build support are not assumed equivalent. Update the ecosystem list and evidence deliberately when repository targets change.

## Capability and runtime limitations

- Required: `text_reasoning`.
- Conditional `web_retrieval`: Required only for current external facts; request supplied sources or label current claims unverified when unavailable.
- Conditional `file_access`: Required for inspecting supplied files; accept pasted content or state extraction limits when unavailable.
- Conditional `persistent_storage`: Required for saving or recalling persistent data; return exportable content or request the actual records when unavailable.
- Fallback: If a required capability is unknown or unavailable, stop the dependent operation, identify missing evidence, and request input or offer manual steps. Do not claim completion.
- Safeguards: Capability declarations never grant authorization. Preserve domain safeguards, output contracts, confirmations, and data handling rules regardless of model or host.

Helpers require actual dependencies, permissions and runtime access. See [`docs/installation.md`](https://github.com/mickpletcher/AI-Skills/blob/main/docs/installation.md) and [`docs/dependencies.md`](https://github.com/mickpletcher/AI-Skills/blob/main/docs/dependencies.md).

## When this master changes

1. Review source, resources, capability/ecosystem declarations and adapters above. Do not widen support just because a model can read Markdown.
2. Run `python tools/skill_compatibility.py`, then `python tools/generate_master_skills.py`. Synchronize all listed candidate entry points, supporting resources and provenance. For a newly allowed target, first generate its candidate, refresh this map, then regenerate candidates again.
3. Review each listed existing platform source for an explicitly approved equivalent change. Do not overwrite shipped variants or promote/rebuild their packages automatically from a master update. Review named-model builds separately; profiles cannot widen the allowlist.
4. Run `python tools/skill_compatibility.py --check`, `python tools/generate_master_skills.py --check`, `python tools/skill_repository.py validate` and `python -m unittest discover -s tools/tests -v`. Record actual host/model tests separately before claiming runtime compatibility.
